newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch life insurers aim for guarantee fund.
newsitem.headline: Dutch life insurers aim for guarantee fund.

text.p: Dutch life insurers said on Tuesday they were aiming for a guarantee fund to protect policy-holders when a life insurer gets into financial trouble.

The Dutch sector regulator Verzekeringskamer and the Dutch life insurers' association said the fund should guarantee up to 200 million guilders per insurer or a maximum of 400 million guilders in the event of a limited risk for the fund's contributors.
The plans were presented to Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm in the hope the Dutch government will give the guarantee fund a legal status.
Verzekeringskamer chairman Arend Vermaat said insurers had a social responsibility to limit the risk for policy holders.
"It is also important for our image," he said.
Some 13,000 Dutch policy-holders lost the majority of their investments when life insurer Vie d'Or was declared bankrupt.
Vermaat said the United Kingdom and Ireland were the only European countries with a system similar to the guarantee fund envisaged by the Dutch insurers.
"Other countries in Europe do not have such a regulation yet," he said.
Vermaat said the life insurance sector was under increasing pressure since the opening up of the European market had stepped up competition.
